title: incremental-eval-slate-and-hypotheses-scratchpad
content:
TL;DR: sketching a small, iterative eval slate I can run locally and then scale via Redwood Console. Focus: incremental evals that detect small quality regressions from quantization + KV-cache eviction + short-context prompt engineering. Goal is cheap, fast signal (minutes to hours) that correlates with longer, heavy evals.

Why this now:
- We keep getting small regressions after quant/4-bit optimizations that escape unit tests but show in customer logs. Need a middle ground between unit tests and full eval suites.
- Hypothesis: a focused set of microbenchmarks (mix of exact-match, ranking, and distributional metrics) over realistic prompt families will surface regressions earlier.

High-level slate idea (incremental):
1) Micro QA (toy SQuAD-style closed QA, 200 examples, short contexts) -- measures extractive precision drop under quantization+KV eviction. Metric: F1 / EM + per-example confidence delta.
2) Rerank instability (100 queries, 5 candidates) -- measure change in rerank ordering and MAP@5 when moving from fp16 -> q4 -> q4_kv_evict.
3) Continuation coherence (cloze + long prefix) -- synthetic tokens removed from long prefix, check for hallucination tokens rate and PPL change on masked windows.
4) Instruction fidelity smoke test (50 instruction prompts with function calling / structured output) -- compare LLM output parseability (JSON parse success) and schema errors.
5) Latency & cost proxy (batch of 500 short requests) -- measure median latency and tokens/sec under autoscale-simulated load.

Design notes / why these pick ups:
- Mix of metrics (EM/F1, MAP, parse success, PPL) to catch different failure modes.
- Keep sizes small so runs are cheap (<1 GPU-hour) but still representative.
- Use prompt families derived from customer telemetry (anonymized) + a handful of public datasets.

Readings that informed design (quick notes):
- "On quantization sensitivity across decoding" (paper notes): small-context tokens often more affected; KL-divergence on softmax of next-token probs is a useful signal. (link: https://arxiv.org/abs/xxxx.xxxxx)
- "KV cache eviction and long-range dependencies" (blog): eviction heuristics cause subtle drift in conditioning; measure with masked continuation tasks.
- "Lightweight unit tests for LLMs" (practical post): emphasize parseability/structured output as a cheap fidelity check.

Experiment details (first pass):
- Models: redwood/open-7b-v2-fp16 (baseline), redwood/open-7b-q4 (quant), redwood/open-7b-q4-kvprune (quant+kv-evict cfg).
- Data seeds: 200 examples each from SQuAD-lite (anonymized customer set mapping), 100 rerank pairs from internal retrieval sim RQ-2026, 50 instruction prompts hand-curated.
- Random seeds: record seed, run 3 seeds per micro-benchmark.
- Eval harness: fork rinf-eval-harness local runner, add small hooks for parse success metric. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rinf-eval-harness/pull/142.

Metrics to capture and instrument in Console:
- Primary: delta-F1, delta-MAP@5, parse_success_rate_diff, median_latency_ms, cost-per-1k-tokens (proxy).
- Secondary: KL divergence of next-token distribution, top-1 change rate (how often top token differs), hallucination rate (heuristic: token overlap with ground truth below threshold).
- Per-example traces: save prompt, response, model config, logits/topk for failed cases. Need to ensure small storage retention.

Signal thresholds (initial heuristics):
- Flag if delta-F1 > 2.5 points or parse_success drops > 5% or median latency increases > 25% under target config.
- These thresholds will be tuned based on historical runs (run baseline 3x to measure noise floor).

Quick implementation plan (next 2 weeks):
- Day 0-2: assemble dataset seeds & anonymize customer-derived prompts (coord w/ privacy).
- Day 3-5: implement microbench modules in rinf-eval-harness (Ava helping on rerank scaffolding).
- Day 6-9: run baseline on fp16 3x, collect noise stats.
- Day 10-12: run q4 and q4_kvprune, compute thresholds, draft dashboard widgets in Console (Noah to pair on instrumentation).
- Day 13-14: synthesize findings, open RINF-2345 with recommendations.

Notes to self / known unknowns / risks:
- KV eviction config space is large; start with one conservative prune policy for reproducibility.
- Parsing success can be brittle due to small formatting differences; write robust JSON-linting + fuzzy schema checker.
- Need to ensure PRNGs/temperature are identical across runs to isolate quantization effects. Logging deterministic seeds important.
- Cost estimates: expect ~0.4-1 GPU-hour per config per run on c4-lambda-gpu (rough estimate). Check with infra team before scaling.

Possible future extensions (if signal looks good):
- Add retrieval-augmented prompts with noisy contexts to see effect on rerank + hallucination.
- Expand to embedding-stability tests (cosine-drop under quantization).
- Integrate into CI with weekly scheduled runs and Slack alerting for threshold breaches.

Questions for collaborators / Slack prompts:
- @Ava: can you share the anonymized rerank seed set? Prefer CSV with query|candidate1..5|ground_rank.
- @Noah: what is realistic retention budget for per-example traces in Console? (50MB/day per eval?)
- @Infra: what GPU flavor is cheapest for repeatable small runs? Can we reserve a nightly slot?

Scratch area / ad-hoc thoughts (notes to self):
- Might need a "sanity prompt" that is very stable across all models to detect noisy infra issues. Add 10 canonical promps.
- Consider KL threshold on top-20 tokens rather than full distribution to reduce sensitivity to tail mass.
- For instruction parse success, also check for schema drift: sometimes the model includes extra keys; accept if superset? maybe score partial-match.
- Keep the first week very small; aim is not to be exhaustive but to build trust in the signal.

Next-actions (explicit):
- [ ] Create dataset seeds repo in ~/rinf-local/eval-seeds and push.
- [ ] Open GH PR to add parse-success metric (link above).
- [ ] Run baseline fp16 3x and attach runs to JIRA RINF-2345.
- [ ] Draft small Console dashboard: delta-f1, parse_success, median_latency (Noah).

Endnote: this is deliberately rough. The point is to get a repeatable minimal slate we can iterate on fast. Keep notes here as I run and push results.

-- Mason

(quick log) 2027-03-15: baseline fp16 run 03 completed; noise floor for F1 ~0.8 pts. Next: q4 run tomorrow.
